units.text: You can use ⟦0⟧ to merge two files of C source code. The output of ⟦1⟧ in this format contains all the lines of both files. Lines common to both files are output just once; the differing parts are separated by the C preprocessor directives ⟦2⟧ or ⟦3⟧, ⟦4⟧, and ⟦5⟧. When compiling the output, you select which version to use by either defining or leaving undefined the macro ⟦6⟧.
units.sourceHTML: You can use diff to merge two files of C source code. The output of diff in this format contains all the lines of both files. Lines common to both files are output just once; the differing parts are separated by the C preprocessor directives #ifdef name or #ifndef name, #else, and #endif. When compiling the output, you select which version to use by either defining or leaving undefined the macro name.

units.text: To merge two files, use ⟦0⟧ with the ⟦1⟧ or ⟦2⟧ option. The argument ⟦3⟧ is the C preprocessor identifier to use in the ⟦4⟧ and ⟦5⟧ directives.
units.sourceHTML: To merge two files, use diff with the -D name or --ifdef=name option. The argument name is the C preprocessor identifier to use in the #ifdef and #ifndef directives.
